rules_en: Budget and costs are per year: running cost plus set-up cost spread over 5 years. Costs are assumptions unless the action says otherwise.

Objective 'curative': the plan maximises extra patients a year treated with curative intent. The other objectives can be chosen: 'deaths' = deaths avoided a year (within five years, per yearly cohort of patients); 'gap' = extra patients a year treated with curative intent, counted only in counties below the national share and only up to it.
Method: buy the measure that adds most to the objective per euro, re-calculate what every other measure would add, and repeat until nothing more fits the budget or nothing more adds anything.
Measures with low-confidence evidence are ranked at 0.5 of their modelled value. They can still be bought; the numbers shown for them are not halved.
A treatment-access measure adds (its effect in percentage points / 100) x the county's patients a year. Every such effect is an assumption with a lower bound of zero: no trial has measured it.

Ceiling: in a county these measures together can add at most 50% of its measured shortfall to the curative share of the best quarter of counties, split into a surgery part and a radiotherapy part as on the care path. The rest is left for what they do not touch (stage at diagnosis, other illness, patient choice); no public table splits the shortfall by reason. A county at or above the best quarter gets no modelled gain.

Video MDT and the surgeon's second opinion count only where the county's own hospital is not a university hospital (not in Helsinki, the four Uusimaa counties, Southwest Finland, Pirkanmaa, North Savo, North Ostrobothnia; our reading of the collaborative-area structure). Travel support is scaled by road distance to the university hospital: 0 at 50 km, full at 200 km.

Where the care path carries a recording flag ('no treatment on record' far above and life-prolonging treatment far below the national share, or almost no drug treatment recorded), the recording audit is bought first. It adds no patients.
Measures that need a national decision (low-dose CT screening) are never bought from a county budget. They are listed under needs_national_decision with their own cost and effect, outside the budget.
Screening is counted from the people screened: participants x their lung cancer death rate without screening x the trial effect. The cost pays for the same participants.

Deaths avoided through treatment access = extra patients treated to cure x 0.15 (0.05-0.3) deaths within five years avoided per patient. This is an assumption, not a causal estimate (see parameters.json, curative_access).

Deaths avoided through days saved use the published hazard ratio per four weeks of delay (Hanna, BMJ 2020), for patients treated with curative intent only; its interval includes no effect, so a lower bound can be below zero.

Overlap: of several pre-diagnosis or mortality measures in one county, the k-th largest counts for 0.7^k of itself; two measures on the same pathway step do not add up, and no step goes below the best Nordic benchmark.
No plan may claim more than 50% of an area's lung cancer deaths.

Stop rule: a measure is not bought if, added to the plan, it costs more than EUR 1,000,000 a year per death avoided a year at its central estimate. The limit is our assumption (Finland has no official one; it is roughly EUR 100,000 per life-year if ten life-years are gained). Such measures are listed as poor_value, and money may be left over.

Each action's numbers are what it adds to the actions ranked before it, so they add up to the plan total. Range, not a probability interval: lowest and highest value when every effect size and conversion assumption is moved together from its lower bound to its upper bound. The point estimate uses the published or central values.

Not counted: a symptom campaign or screening would also raise the share treated to cure by finding cancers earlier; the model counts them only through deaths avoided. Earlier life-prolonging drug treatment is not counted at all.
No budget share is reserved for any kind of measure (the 25% pathway rule of the earlier version is removed).
500000.saturation_note_en: EUR 61,690 a year buys every measure that adds to this objective in North Savo. The remaining EUR 438,310 buys nothing more in the model: the access measures are limited by the reachable part of the measured shortfall, not by money. To see what else the money could do, choose the deaths objective (pathway measures) or look at the measures that need a national decision.

goal3_link.note_en: Lung cancer causes about 93 deaths a year in North Savo (Finnish Cancer Registry, 2020-2024). This plan is modelled to avoid 0.2 of them a year (0.0-0.7), about 0.24%. Goal 3 of the cancer strategy asks for 10% lower cancer mortality (all cancers: from 13,288 deaths in 2022), so a plan of this size is a small part of it. The strategy also wants lung cancer survival at the level of Sweden and Norway: five-year survival is 13.2 points lower for Finnish men and 7.8 for women (2020-2024, NORDCAN). The share of patients treated with curative intent is the part of that gap a county can act on after diagnosis; this plan adds 1.5 such patients a year. Deaths avoided are modelled from stated assumptions, not observed.

rules_en: Budget and costs are per year: running cost plus set-up cost spread over 5 years. Costs are assumptions unless the action says otherwise.

Objective 'curative': the plan maximises extra patients a year treated with curative intent. The other objectives can be chosen: 'deaths' = deaths avoided a year (within five years, per yearly cohort of patients); 'gap' = extra patients a year treated with curative intent, counted only in counties below the national share and only up to it.
Method: buy the measure that adds most to the objective per euro, re-calculate what every other measure would add, and repeat until nothing more fits the budget or nothing more adds anything.
Measures with low-confidence evidence are ranked at 0.5 of their modelled value. They can still be bought; the numbers shown for them are not halved.
A treatment-access measure adds (its effect in percentage points / 100) x the county's patients a year. Every such effect is an assumption with a lower bound of zero: no trial has measured it.

Ceiling: in a county these measures together can add at most 50% of its measured shortfall to the curative share of the best quarter of counties, split into a surgery part and a radiotherapy part as on the care path. The rest is left for what they do not touch (stage at diagnosis, other illness, patient choice); no public table splits the shortfall by reason. A county at or above the best quarter gets no modelled gain.

Video MDT and the surgeon's second opinion count only where the county's own hospital is not a university hospital (not in Helsinki, the four Uusimaa counties, Southwest Finland, Pirkanmaa, North Savo, North Ostrobothnia; our reading of the collaborative-area structure). Travel support is scaled by road distance to the university hospital: 0 at 50 km, full at 200 km.

Where the care path carries a recording flag ('no treatment on record' far above and life-prolonging treatment far below the national share, or almost no drug treatment recorded), the recording audit is bought first. It adds no patients.
Measures that need a national decision (low-dose CT screening) are never bought from a county budget. They are listed under needs_national_decision with their own cost and effect, outside the budget.
Screening is counted from the people screened: participants x their lung cancer death rate without screening x the trial effect. The cost pays for the same participants.

Deaths avoided through treatment access = extra patients treated to cure x 0.15 (0.05-0.3) deaths within five years avoided per patient. This is an assumption, not a causal estimate (see parameters.json, curative_access).

Deaths avoided through days saved use the published hazard ratio per four weeks of delay (Hanna, BMJ 2020), for patients treated with curative intent only; its interval includes no effect, so a lower bound can be below zero.

Overlap: of several pre-diagnosis or mortality measures in one county, the k-th largest counts for 0.7^k of itself; two measures on the same pathway step do not add up, and no step goes below the best Nordic benchmark.
No plan may claim more than 50% of an area's lung cancer deaths.

Stop rule: a measure is not bought if, added to the plan, it costs more than EUR 1,000,000 a year per death avoided a year at its central estimate. The limit is our assumption (Finland has no official one; it is roughly EUR 100,000 per life-year if ten life-years are gained). Such measures are listed as poor_value, and money may be left over.

Each action's numbers are what it adds to the actions ranked before it, so they add up to the plan total. Range, not a probability interval: lowest and highest value when every effect size and conversion assumption is moved together from its lower bound to its upper bound. The point estimate uses the published or central values.

Not counted: a symptom campaign or screening would also raise the share treated to cure by finding cancers earlier; the model counts them only through deaths avoided. Earlier life-prolonging drug treatment is not counted at all.
No budget share is reserved for any kind of measure (the 25% pathway rule of the earlier version is removed).
2000000.saturation_note_en: EUR 61,690 a year buys every measure that adds to this objective in North Savo. The remaining EUR 1,938,310 buys nothing more in the model: the access measures are limited by the reachable part of the measured shortfall, not by money. To see what else the money could do, choose the deaths objective (pathway measures) or look at the measures that need a national decision.

goal3_link.note_en: Lung cancer causes about 93 deaths a year in North Savo (Finnish Cancer Registry, 2020-2024). This plan is modelled to avoid 0.2 of them a year (0.0-0.7), about 0.24%. Goal 3 of the cancer strategy asks for 10% lower cancer mortality (all cancers: from 13,288 deaths in 2022), so a plan of this size is a small part of it. The strategy also wants lung cancer survival at the level of Sweden and Norway: five-year survival is 13.2 points lower for Finnish men and 7.8 for women (2020-2024, NORDCAN). The share of patients treated with curative intent is the part of that gap a county can act on after diagnosis; this plan adds 1.5 such patients a year. Deaths avoided are modelled from stated assumptions, not observed.

rules_en: Budget and costs are per year: running cost plus set-up cost spread over 5 years. Costs are assumptions unless the action says otherwise.

Objective 'curative': the plan maximises extra patients a year treated with curative intent. The other objectives can be chosen: 'deaths' = deaths avoided a year (within five years, per yearly cohort of patients); 'gap' = extra patients a year treated with curative intent, counted only in counties below the national share and only up to it.
Method: buy the measure that adds most to the objective per euro, re-calculate what every other measure would add, and repeat until nothing more fits the budget or nothing more adds anything.
Measures with low-confidence evidence are ranked at 0.5 of their modelled value. They can still be bought; the numbers shown for them are not halved.
A treatment-access measure adds (its effect in percentage points / 100) x the county's patients a year. Every such effect is an assumption with a lower bound of zero: no trial has measured it.

Ceiling: in a county these measures together can add at most 50% of its measured shortfall to the curative share of the best quarter of counties, split into a surgery part and a radiotherapy part as on the care path. The rest is left for what they do not touch (stage at diagnosis, other illness, patient choice); no public table splits the shortfall by reason. A county at or above the best quarter gets no modelled gain.

Video MDT and the surgeon's second opinion count only where the county's own hospital is not a university hospital (not in Helsinki, the four Uusimaa counties, Southwest Finland, Pirkanmaa, North Savo, North Ostrobothnia; our reading of the collaborative-area structure). Travel support is scaled by road distance to the university hospital: 0 at 50 km, full at 200 km.

Where the care path carries a recording flag ('no treatment on record' far above and life-prolonging treatment far below the national share, or almost no drug treatment recorded), the recording audit is bought first. It adds no patients.
Measures that need a national decision (low-dose CT screening) are never bought from a county budget. They are listed under needs_national_decision with their own cost and effect, outside the budget.
Screening is counted from the people screened: participants x their lung cancer death rate without screening x the trial effect. The cost pays for the same participants.

Deaths avoided through treatment access = extra patients treated to cure x 0.15 (0.05-0.3) deaths within five years avoided per patient. This is an assumption, not a causal estimate (see parameters.json, curative_access).

Deaths avoided through days saved use the published hazard ratio per four weeks of delay (Hanna, BMJ 2020), for patients treated with curative intent only; its interval includes no effect, so a lower bound can be below zero.

Overlap: of several pre-diagnosis or mortality measures in one county, the k-th largest counts for 0.7^k of itself; two measures on the same pathway step do not add up, and no step goes below the best Nordic benchmark.
No plan may claim more than 50% of an area's lung cancer deaths.

Stop rule: a measure is not bought if, added to the plan, it costs more than EUR 1,000,000 a year per death avoided a year at its central estimate. The limit is our assumption (Finland has no official one; it is roughly EUR 100,000 per life-year if ten life-years are gained). Such measures are listed as poor_value, and money may be left over.

Each action's numbers are what it adds to the actions ranked before it, so they add up to the plan total. Range, not a probability interval: lowest and highest value when every effect size and conversion assumption is moved together from its lower bound to its upper bound. The point estimate uses the published or central values.

Not counted: a symptom campaign or screening would also raise the share treated to cure by finding cancers earlier; the model counts them only through deaths avoided. Earlier life-prolonging drug treatment is not counted at all.
No budget share is reserved for any kind of measure (the 25% pathway rule of the earlier version is removed).
10000000.saturation_note_en: EUR 61,690 a year buys every measure that adds to this objective in North Savo. The remaining EUR 9,938,310 buys nothing more in the model: the access measures are limited by the reachable part of the measured shortfall, not by money. To see what else the money could do, choose the deaths objective (pathway measures) or look at the measures that need a national decision.

goal3_link.note_en: Lung cancer causes about 93 deaths a year in North Savo (Finnish Cancer Registry, 2020-2024). This plan is modelled to avoid 0.2 of them a year (0.0-0.7), about 0.24%. Goal 3 of the cancer strategy asks for 10% lower cancer mortality (all cancers: from 13,288 deaths in 2022), so a plan of this size is a small part of it. The strategy also wants lung cancer survival at the level of Sweden and Norway: five-year survival is 13.2 points lower for Finnish men and 7.8 for women (2020-2024, NORDCAN). The share of patients treated with curative intent is the part of that gap a county can act on after diagnosis; this plan adds 1.5 such patients a year. Deaths avoided are modelled from stated assumptions, not observed.

rules_en: Budget and costs are per year: running cost plus set-up cost spread over 5 years. Costs are assumptions unless the action says otherwise.

Objective 'curative': the plan maximises extra patients a year treated with curative intent. The other objectives can be chosen: 'deaths' = deaths avoided a year (within five years, per yearly cohort of patients); 'gap' = extra patients a year treated with curative intent, counted only in counties below the national share and only up to it.
Method: buy the measure that adds most to the objective per euro, re-calculate what every other measure would add, and repeat until nothing more fits the budget or nothing more adds anything.
Measures with low-confidence evidence are ranked at 0.5 of their modelled value. They can still be bought; the numbers shown for them are not halved.
A treatment-access measure adds (its effect in percentage points / 100) x the county's patients a year. Every such effect is an assumption with a lower bound of zero: no trial has measured it.

Ceiling: in a county these measures together can add at most 50% of its measured shortfall to the curative share of the best quarter of counties, split into a surgery part and a radiotherapy part as on the care path. The rest is left for what they do not touch (stage at diagnosis, other illness, patient choice); no public table splits the shortfall by reason. A county at or above the best quarter gets no modelled gain.

Video MDT and the surgeon's second opinion count only where the county's own hospital is not a university hospital (not in Helsinki, the four Uusimaa counties, Southwest Finland, Pirkanmaa, North Savo, North Ostrobothnia; our reading of the collaborative-area structure). Travel support is scaled by road distance to the university hospital: 0 at 50 km, full at 200 km.

Where the care path carries a recording flag ('no treatment on record' far above and life-prolonging treatment far below the national share, or almost no drug treatment recorded), the recording audit is bought first. It adds no patients.
Measures that need a national decision (low-dose CT screening) are never bought from a county budget. They are listed under needs_national_decision with their own cost and effect, outside the budget.
Screening is counted from the people screened: participants x their lung cancer death rate without screening x the trial effect. The cost pays for the same participants.

Deaths avoided through treatment access = extra patients treated to cure x 0.15 (0.05-0.3) deaths within five years avoided per patient. This is an assumption, not a causal estimate (see parameters.json, curative_access).

Deaths avoided through days saved use the published hazard ratio per four weeks of delay (Hanna, BMJ 2020), for patients treated with curative intent only; its interval includes no effect, so a lower bound can be below zero.

Overlap: of several pre-diagnosis or mortality measures in one county, the k-th largest counts for 0.7^k of itself; two measures on the same pathway step do not add up, and no step goes below the best Nordic benchmark.
No plan may claim more than 50% of an area's lung cancer deaths.

Stop rule: a measure is not bought if, added to the plan, it costs more than EUR 1,000,000 a year per death avoided a year at its central estimate. The limit is our assumption (Finland has no official one; it is roughly EUR 100,000 per life-year if ten life-years are gained). Such measures are listed as poor_value, and money may be left over.

Each action's numbers are what it adds to the actions ranked before it, so they add up to the plan total. Range, not a probability interval: lowest and highest value when every effect size and conversion assumption is moved together from its lower bound to its upper bound. The point estimate uses the published or central values.

Not counted: a symptom campaign or screening would also raise the share treated to cure by finding cancers earlier; the model counts them only through deaths avoided. Earlier life-prolonging drug treatment is not counted at all.
No budget share is reserved for any kind of measure (the 25% pathway rule of the earlier version is removed).
250000.saturation_note_en: EUR 61,690 a year buys every measure that adds to this objective in North Savo. The remaining EUR 188,310 buys nothing more in the model: the access measures are limited by the reachable part of the measured shortfall, not by money. To see what else the money could do, choose the deaths objective (pathway measures) or look at the measures that need a national decision.

goal3_link.note_en: Lung cancer causes about 93 deaths a year in North Savo (Finnish Cancer Registry, 2020-2024). This plan is modelled to avoid 0.2 of them a year (0.0-0.7), about 0.24%. Goal 3 of the cancer strategy asks for 10% lower cancer mortality (all cancers: from 13,288 deaths in 2022), so a plan of this size is a small part of it. The strategy also wants lung cancer survival at the level of Sweden and Norway: five-year survival is 13.2 points lower for Finnish men and 7.8 for women (2020-2024, NORDCAN). The share of patients treated with curative intent is the part of that gap a county can act on after diagnosis; this plan adds 1.5 such patients a year. Deaths avoided are modelled from stated assumptions, not observed.

rules_en: Budget and costs are per year: running cost plus set-up cost spread over 5 years. Costs are assumptions unless the action says otherwise.

Objective 'curative': the plan maximises extra patients a year treated with curative intent. The other objectives can be chosen: 'deaths' = deaths avoided a year (within five years, per yearly cohort of patients); 'gap' = extra patients a year treated with curative intent, counted only in counties below the national share and only up to it.
Method: buy the measure that adds most to the objective per euro, re-calculate what every other measure would add, and repeat until nothing more fits the budget or nothing more adds anything.
Measures with low-confidence evidence are ranked at 0.5 of their modelled value. They can still be bought; the numbers shown for them are not halved.
A treatment-access measure adds (its effect in percentage points / 100) x the county's patients a year. Every such effect is an assumption with a lower bound of zero: no trial has measured it.

Ceiling: in a county these measures together can add at most 50% of its measured shortfall to the curative share of the best quarter of counties, split into a surgery part and a radiotherapy part as on the care path. The rest is left for what they do not touch (stage at diagnosis, other illness, patient choice); no public table splits the shortfall by reason. A county at or above the best quarter gets no modelled gain.

Video MDT and the surgeon's second opinion count only where the county's own hospital is not a university hospital (not in Helsinki, the four Uusimaa counties, Southwest Finland, Pirkanmaa, North Savo, North Ostrobothnia; our reading of the collaborative-area structure). Travel support is scaled by road distance to the university hospital: 0 at 50 km, full at 200 km.

Where the care path carries a recording flag ('no treatment on record' far above and life-prolonging treatment far below the national share, or almost no drug treatment recorded), the recording audit is bought first. It adds no patients.
Measures that need a national decision (low-dose CT screening) are never bought from a county budget. They are listed under needs_national_decision with their own cost and effect, outside the budget.
Screening is counted from the people screened: participants x their lung cancer death rate without screening x the trial effect. The cost pays for the same participants.

Deaths avoided through treatment access = extra patients treated to cure x 0.15 (0.05-0.3) deaths within five years avoided per patient. This is an assumption, not a causal estimate (see parameters.json, curative_access).

Deaths avoided through days saved use the published hazard ratio per four weeks of delay (Hanna, BMJ 2020), for patients treated with curative intent only; its interval includes no effect, so a lower bound can be below zero.

Overlap: of several pre-diagnosis or mortality measures in one county, the k-th largest counts for 0.7^k of itself; two measures on the same pathway step do not add up, and no step goes below the best Nordic benchmark.
No plan may claim more than 50% of an area's lung cancer deaths.

Stop rule: a measure is not bought if, added to the plan, it costs more than EUR 1,000,000 a year per death avoided a year at its central estimate. The limit is our assumption (Finland has no official one; it is roughly EUR 100,000 per life-year if ten life-years are gained). Such measures are listed as poor_value, and money may be left over.

Each action's numbers are what it adds to the actions ranked before it, so they add up to the plan total. Range, not a probability interval: lowest and highest value when every effect size and conversion assumption is moved together from its lower bound to its upper bound. The point estimate uses the published or central values.

Not counted: a symptom campaign or screening would also raise the share treated to cure by finding cancers earlier; the model counts them only through deaths avoided. Earlier life-prolonging drug treatment is not counted at all.
No budget share is reserved for any kind of measure (the 25% pathway rule of the earlier version is removed).
1000000.saturation_note_en: EUR 61,690 a year buys every measure that adds to this objective in North Savo. The remaining EUR 938,310 buys nothing more in the model: the access measures are limited by the reachable part of the measured shortfall, not by money. To see what else the money could do, choose the deaths objective (pathway measures) or look at the measures that need a national decision.

goal3_link.note_en: Lung cancer causes about 93 deaths a year in North Savo (Finnish Cancer Registry, 2020-2024). This plan is modelled to avoid 0.2 of them a year (0.0-0.7), about 0.24%. Goal 3 of the cancer strategy asks for 10% lower cancer mortality (all cancers: from 13,288 deaths in 2022), so a plan of this size is a small part of it. The strategy also wants lung cancer survival at the level of Sweden and Norway: five-year survival is 13.2 points lower for Finnish men and 7.8 for women (2020-2024, NORDCAN). The share of patients treated with curative intent is the part of that gap a county can act on after diagnosis; this plan adds 1.5 such patients a year. Deaths avoided are modelled from stated assumptions, not observed.

rules_en: Budget and costs are per year: running cost plus set-up cost spread over 5 years. Costs are assumptions unless the action says otherwise.

Objective 'curative': the plan maximises extra patients a year treated with curative intent. The other objectives can be chosen: 'deaths' = deaths avoided a year (within five years, per yearly cohort of patients); 'gap' = extra patients a year treated with curative intent, counted only in counties below the national share and only up to it.
Method: buy the measure that adds most to the objective per euro, re-calculate what every other measure would add, and repeat until nothing more fits the budget or nothing more adds anything.
Measures with low-confidence evidence are ranked at 0.5 of their modelled value. They can still be bought; the numbers shown for them are not halved.
A treatment-access measure adds (its effect in percentage points / 100) x the county's patients a year. Every such effect is an assumption with a lower bound of zero: no trial has measured it.

Ceiling: in a county these measures together can add at most 50% of its measured shortfall to the curative share of the best quarter of counties, split into a surgery part and a radiotherapy part as on the care path. The rest is left for what they do not touch (stage at diagnosis, other illness, patient choice); no public table splits the shortfall by reason. A county at or above the best quarter gets no modelled gain.

Video MDT and the surgeon's second opinion count only where the county's own hospital is not a university hospital (not in Helsinki, the four Uusimaa counties, Southwest Finland, Pirkanmaa, North Savo, North Ostrobothnia; our reading of the collaborative-area structure). Travel support is scaled by road distance to the university hospital: 0 at 50 km, full at 200 km.

Where the care path carries a recording flag ('no treatment on record' far above and life-prolonging treatment far below the national share, or almost no drug treatment recorded), the recording audit is bought first. It adds no patients.
Measures that need a national decision (low-dose CT screening) are never bought from a county budget. They are listed under needs_national_decision with their own cost and effect, outside the budget.
Screening is counted from the people screened: participants x their lung cancer death rate without screening x the trial effect. The cost pays for the same participants.

Deaths avoided through treatment access = extra patients treated to cure x 0.15 (0.05-0.3) deaths within five years avoided per patient. This is an assumption, not a causal estimate (see parameters.json, curative_access).

Deaths avoided through days saved use the published hazard ratio per four weeks of delay (Hanna, BMJ 2020), for patients treated with curative intent only; its interval includes no effect, so a lower bound can be below zero.

Overlap: of several pre-diagnosis or mortality measures in one county, the k-th largest counts for 0.7^k of itself; two measures on the same pathway step do not add up, and no step goes below the best Nordic benchmark.
No plan may claim more than 50% of an area's lung cancer deaths.

Stop rule: a measure is not bought if, added to the plan, it costs more than EUR 1,000,000 a year per death avoided a year at its central estimate. The limit is our assumption (Finland has no official one; it is roughly EUR 100,000 per life-year if ten life-years are gained). Such measures are listed as poor_value, and money may be left over.

Each action's numbers are what it adds to the actions ranked before it, so they add up to the plan total. Range, not a probability interval: lowest and highest value when every effect size and conversion assumption is moved together from its lower bound to its upper bound. The point estimate uses the published or central values.

Not counted: a symptom campaign or screening would also raise the share treated to cure by finding cancers earlier; the model counts them only through deaths avoided. Earlier life-prolonging drug treatment is not counted at all.
No budget share is reserved for any kind of measure (the 25% pathway rule of the earlier version is removed).
5000000.saturation_note_en: EUR 61,690 a year buys every measure that adds to this objective in North Savo. The remaining EUR 4,938,310 buys nothing more in the model: the access measures are limited by the reachable part of the measured shortfall, not by money. To see what else the money could do, choose the deaths objective (pathway measures) or look at the measures that need a national decision.

goal3_link.note_en: Lung cancer causes about 93 deaths a year in North Savo (Finnish Cancer Registry, 2020-2024). This plan is modelled to avoid 0.2 of them a year (0.0-0.7), about 0.24%. Goal 3 of the cancer strategy asks for 10% lower cancer mortality (all cancers: from 13,288 deaths in 2022), so a plan of this size is a small part of it. The strategy also wants lung cancer survival at the level of Sweden and Norway: five-year survival is 13.2 points lower for Finnish men and 7.8 for women (2020-2024, NORDCAN). The share of patients treated with curative intent is the part of that gap a county can act on after diagnosis; this plan adds 1.5 such patients a year. Deaths avoided are modelled from stated assumptions, not observed.

rules_en: Budget and costs are per year: running cost plus set-up cost spread over 5 years. Costs are assumptions unless the action says otherwise.

Objective 'deaths': the plan maximises deaths avoided a year (within five years, per yearly cohort of patients). The other objectives can be chosen: 'curative' = extra patients a year treated with curative intent; 'gap' = extra patients a year treated with curative intent, counted only in counties below the national share and only up to it.
Method: buy the measure that adds most to the objective per euro, re-calculate what every other measure would add, and repeat until nothing more fits the budget or nothing more adds anything.
Measures with low-confidence evidence are ranked at 0.5 of their modelled value. They can still be bought; the numbers shown for them are not halved.
A treatment-access measure adds (its effect in percentage points / 100) x the county's patients a year. Every such effect is an assumption with a lower bound of zero: no trial has measured it.

Ceiling: in a county these measures together can add at most 50% of its measured shortfall to the curative share of the best quarter of counties, split into a surgery part and a radiotherapy part as on the care path. The rest is left for what they do not touch (stage at diagnosis, other illness, patient choice); no public table splits the shortfall by reason. A county at or above the best quarter gets no modelled gain.

Video MDT and the surgeon's second opinion count only where the county's own hospital is not a university hospital (not in Helsinki, the four Uusimaa counties, Southwest Finland, Pirkanmaa, North Savo, North Ostrobothnia; our reading of the collaborative-area structure). Travel support is scaled by road distance to the university hospital: 0 at 50 km, full at 200 km.

Where the care path carries a recording flag ('no treatment on record' far above and life-prolonging treatment far below the national share, or almost no drug treatment recorded), the recording audit is bought first. It adds no patients.
Measures that need a national decision (low-dose CT screening) are never bought from a county budget. They are listed under needs_national_decision with their own cost and effect, outside the budget.
Screening is counted from the people screened: participants x their lung cancer death rate without screening x the trial effect. The cost pays for the same participants.

Deaths avoided through treatment access = extra patients treated to cure x 0.15 (0.05-0.3) deaths within five years avoided per patient. This is an assumption, not a causal estimate (see parameters.json, curative_access).

Deaths avoided through days saved use the published hazard ratio per four weeks of delay (Hanna, BMJ 2020), for patients treated with curative intent only; its interval includes no effect, so a lower bound can be below zero.

Overlap: of several pre-diagnosis or mortality measures in one county, the k-th largest counts for 0.7^k of itself; two measures on the same pathway step do not add up, and no step goes below the best Nordic benchmark.
No plan may claim more than 50% of an area's lung cancer deaths.

Stop rule: a measure is not bought if, added to the plan, it costs more than EUR 1,000,000 a year per death avoided a year at its central estimate. The limit is our assumption (Finland has no official one; it is roughly EUR 100,000 per life-year if ten life-years are gained). Such measures are listed as poor_value, and money may be left over.

Each action's numbers are what it adds to the actions ranked before it, so they add up to the plan total. Range, not a probability interval: lowest and highest value when every effect size and conversion assumption is moved together from its lower bound to its upper bound. The point estimate uses the published or central values.

Not counted: a symptom campaign or screening would also raise the share treated to cure by finding cancers earlier; the model counts them only through deaths avoided. Earlier life-prolonging drug treatment is not counted at all.
No budget share is reserved for any kind of measure (the 25% pathway rule of the earlier version is removed).
100000.saturation_note_en: Not saturated: the cheapest measure that would still add something (Reflex molecular testing ordered by pathology) needs EUR 23,230 a year; EUR 20,080 is left.

goal3_link.note_en: Lung cancer causes about 93 deaths a year in North Savo (Finnish Cancer Registry, 2020-2024). This plan is modelled to avoid 0.6 of them a year (0.1-1.2), about 0.59%. Goal 3 of the cancer strategy asks for 10% lower cancer mortality (all cancers: from 13,288 deaths in 2022), so a plan of this size is a small part of it. The strategy also wants lung cancer survival at the level of Sweden and Norway: five-year survival is 13.2 points lower for Finnish men and 7.8 for women (2020-2024, NORDCAN). The share of patients treated with curative intent is the part of that gap a county can act on after diagnosis; this plan adds 1.0 such patients a year. Deaths avoided are modelled from stated assumptions, not observed.

rules_en: Budget and costs are per year: running cost plus set-up cost spread over 5 years. Costs are assumptions unless the action says otherwise.

Objective 'deaths': the plan maximises deaths avoided a year (within five years, per yearly cohort of patients). The other objectives can be chosen: 'curative' = extra patients a year treated with curative intent; 'gap' = extra patients a year treated with curative intent, counted only in counties below the national share and only up to it.
Method: buy the measure that adds most to the objective per euro, re-calculate what every other measure would add, and repeat until nothing more fits the budget or nothing more adds anything.
Measures with low-confidence evidence are ranked at 0.5 of their modelled value. They can still be bought; the numbers shown for them are not halved.
A treatment-access measure adds (its effect in percentage points / 100) x the county's patients a year. Every such effect is an assumption with a lower bound of zero: no trial has measured it.

Ceiling: in a county these measures together can add at most 50% of its measured shortfall to the curative share of the best quarter of counties, split into a surgery part and a radiotherapy part as on the care path. The rest is left for what they do not touch (stage at diagnosis, other illness, patient choice); no public table splits the shortfall by reason. A county at or above the best quarter gets no modelled gain.

Video MDT and the surgeon's second opinion count only where the county's own hospital is not a university hospital (not in Helsinki, the four Uusimaa counties, Southwest Finland, Pirkanmaa, North Savo, North Ostrobothnia; our reading of the collaborative-area structure). Travel support is scaled by road distance to the university hospital: 0 at 50 km, full at 200 km.

Where the care path carries a recording flag ('no treatment on record' far above and life-prolonging treatment far below the national share, or almost no drug treatment recorded), the recording audit is bought first. It adds no patients.
Measures that need a national decision (low-dose CT screening) are never bought from a county budget. They are listed under needs_national_decision with their own cost and effect, outside the budget.
Screening is counted from the people screened: participants x their lung cancer death rate without screening x the trial effect. The cost pays for the same participants.

Deaths avoided through treatment access = extra patients treated to cure x 0.15 (0.05-0.3) deaths within five years avoided per patient. This is an assumption, not a causal estimate (see parameters.json, curative_access).

Deaths avoided through days saved use the published hazard ratio per four weeks of delay (Hanna, BMJ 2020), for patients treated with curative intent only; its interval includes no effect, so a lower bound can be below zero.

Overlap: of several pre-diagnosis or mortality measures in one county, the k-th largest counts for 0.7^k of itself; two measures on the same pathway step do not add up, and no step goes below the best Nordic benchmark.
No plan may claim more than 50% of an area's lung cancer deaths.

Stop rule: a measure is not bought if, added to the plan, it costs more than EUR 1,000,000 a year per death avoided a year at its central estimate. The limit is our assumption (Finland has no official one; it is roughly EUR 100,000 per life-year if ten life-years are gained). Such measures are listed as poor_value, and money may be left over.

Each action's numbers are what it adds to the actions ranked before it, so they add up to the plan total. Range, not a probability interval: lowest and highest value when every effect size and conversion assumption is moved together from its lower bound to its upper bound. The point estimate uses the published or central values.

Not counted: a symptom campaign or screening would also raise the share treated to cure by finding cancers earlier; the model counts them only through deaths avoided. Earlier life-prolonging drug treatment is not counted at all.
No budget share is reserved for any kind of measure (the 25% pathway rule of the earlier version is removed).
500000.saturation_note_en: EUR 283,970 a year buys every measure that adds to this objective in North Savo. The remaining EUR 216,030 buys nothing more in the model: no remaining measure adds deaths avoided at an acceptable cost. Measures above the value limit are listed as poor_value under not_chosen.

goal3_link.note_en: Lung cancer causes about 93 deaths a year in North Savo (Finnish Cancer Registry, 2020-2024). This plan is modelled to avoid 1.1 of them a year (0.1-3.2), about 1.22%. Goal 3 of the cancer strategy asks for 10% lower cancer mortality (all cancers: from 13,288 deaths in 2022), so a plan of this size is a small part of it. The strategy also wants lung cancer survival at the level of Sweden and Norway: five-year survival is 13.2 points lower for Finnish men and 7.8 for women (2020-2024, NORDCAN). The share of patients treated with curative intent is the part of that gap a county can act on after diagnosis; this plan adds 1.5 such patients a year. Deaths avoided are modelled from stated assumptions, not observed.

500000.budget_basis_en: Budget and costs are per year: running cost plus set-up cost spread over 5 years.

rules_en: Budget and costs are per year: running cost plus set-up cost spread over 5 years. Costs are assumptions unless the action says otherwise.

Objective 'deaths': the plan maximises deaths avoided a year (within five years, per yearly cohort of patients). The other objectives can be chosen: 'curative' = extra patients a year treated with curative intent; 'gap' = extra patients a year treated with curative intent, counted only in counties below the national share and only up to it.
Method: buy the measure that adds most to the objective per euro, re-calculate what every other measure would add, and repeat until nothing more fits the budget or nothing more adds anything.
Measures with low-confidence evidence are ranked at 0.5 of their modelled value. They can still be bought; the numbers shown for them are not halved.
A treatment-access measure adds (its effect in percentage points / 100) x the county's patients a year. Every such effect is an assumption with a lower bound of zero: no trial has measured it.

Ceiling: in a county these measures together can add at most 50% of its measured shortfall to the curative share of the best quarter of counties, split into a surgery part and a radiotherapy part as on the care path. The rest is left for what they do not touch (stage at diagnosis, other illness, patient choice); no public table splits the shortfall by reason. A county at or above the best quarter gets no modelled gain.

Video MDT and the surgeon's second opinion count only where the county's own hospital is not a university hospital (not in Helsinki, the four Uusimaa counties, Southwest Finland, Pirkanmaa, North Savo, North Ostrobothnia; our reading of the collaborative-area structure). Travel support is scaled by road distance to the university hospital: 0 at 50 km, full at 200 km.

Where the care path carries a recording flag ('no treatment on record' far above and life-prolonging treatment far below the national share, or almost no drug treatment recorded), the recording audit is bought first. It adds no patients.
Measures that need a national decision (low-dose CT screening) are never bought from a county budget. They are listed under needs_national_decision with their own cost and effect, outside the budget.
Screening is counted from the people screened: participants x their lung cancer death rate without screening x the trial effect. The cost pays for the same participants.

Deaths avoided through treatment access = extra patients treated to cure x 0.15 (0.05-0.3) deaths within five years avoided per patient. This is an assumption, not a causal estimate (see parameters.json, curative_access).

Deaths avoided through days saved use the published hazard ratio per four weeks of delay (Hanna, BMJ 2020), for patients treated with curative intent only; its interval includes no effect, so a lower bound can be below zero.

Overlap: of several pre-diagnosis or mortality measures in one county, the k-th largest counts for 0.7^k of itself; two measures on the same pathway step do not add up, and no step goes below the best Nordic benchmark.
No plan may claim more than 50% of an area's lung cancer deaths.

Stop rule: a measure is not bought if, added to the plan, it costs more than EUR 1,000,000 a year per death avoided a year at its central estimate. The limit is our assumption (Finland has no official one; it is roughly EUR 100,000 per life-year if ten life-years are gained). Such measures are listed as poor_value, and money may be left over.

Each action's numbers are what it adds to the actions ranked before it, so they add up to the plan total. Range, not a probability interval: lowest and highest value when every effect size and conversion assumption is moved together from its lower bound to its upper bound. The point estimate uses the published or central values.

Not counted: a symptom campaign or screening would also raise the share treated to cure by finding cancers earlier; the model counts them only through deaths avoided. Earlier life-prolonging drug treatment is not counted at all.
No budget share is reserved for any kind of measure (the 25% pathway rule of the earlier version is removed).
1000000.saturation_note_en: EUR 283,970 a year buys every measure that adds to this objective in North Savo. The remaining EUR 716,030 buys nothing more in the model: no remaining measure adds deaths avoided at an acceptable cost. Measures above the value limit are listed as poor_value under not_chosen.

goal3_link.note_en: Lung cancer causes about 93 deaths a year in North Savo (Finnish Cancer Registry, 2020-2024). This plan is modelled to avoid 1.1 of them a year (0.1-3.2), about 1.22%. Goal 3 of the cancer strategy asks for 10% lower cancer mortality (all cancers: from 13,288 deaths in 2022), so a plan of this size is a small part of it. The strategy also wants lung cancer survival at the level of Sweden and Norway: five-year survival is 13.2 points lower for Finnish men and 7.8 for women (2020-2024, NORDCAN). The share of patients treated with curative intent is the part of that gap a county can act on after diagnosis; this plan adds 1.5 such patients a year. Deaths avoided are modelled from stated assumptions, not observed.

rules_en: Budget and costs are per year: running cost plus set-up cost spread over 5 years. Costs are assumptions unless the action says otherwise.

Objective 'deaths': the plan maximises deaths avoided a year (within five years, per yearly cohort of patients). The other objectives can be chosen: 'curative' = extra patients a year treated with curative intent; 'gap' = extra patients a year treated with curative intent, counted only in counties below the national share and only up to it.
Method: buy the measure that adds most to the objective per euro, re-calculate what every other measure would add, and repeat until nothing more fits the budget or nothing more adds anything.
Measures with low-confidence evidence are ranked at 0.5 of their modelled value. They can still be bought; the numbers shown for them are not halved.
A treatment-access measure adds (its effect in percentage points / 100) x the county's patients a year. Every such effect is an assumption with a lower bound of zero: no trial has measured it.

Ceiling: in a county these measures together can add at most 50% of its measured shortfall to the curative share of the best quarter of counties, split into a surgery part and a radiotherapy part as on the care path. The rest is left for what they do not touch (stage at diagnosis, other illness, patient choice); no public table splits the shortfall by reason. A county at or above the best quarter gets no modelled gain.

Video MDT and the surgeon's second opinion count only where the county's own hospital is not a university hospital (not in Helsinki, the four Uusimaa counties, Southwest Finland, Pirkanmaa, North Savo, North Ostrobothnia; our reading of the collaborative-area structure). Travel support is scaled by road distance to the university hospital: 0 at 50 km, full at 200 km.

Where the care path carries a recording flag ('no treatment on record' far above and life-prolonging treatment far below the national share, or almost no drug treatment recorded), the recording audit is bought first. It adds no patients.
Measures that need a national decision (low-dose CT screening) are never bought from a county budget. They are listed under needs_national_decision with their own cost and effect, outside the budget.
Screening is counted from the people screened: participants x their lung cancer death rate without screening x the trial effect. The cost pays for the same participants.

Deaths avoided through treatment access = extra patients treated to cure x 0.15 (0.05-0.3) deaths within five years avoided per patient. This is an assumption, not a causal estimate (see parameters.json, curative_access).

Deaths avoided through days saved use the published hazard ratio per four weeks of delay (Hanna, BMJ 2020), for patients treated with curative intent only; its interval includes no effect, so a lower bound can be below zero.

Overlap: of several pre-diagnosis or mortality measures in one county, the k-th largest counts for 0.7^k of itself; two measures on the same pathway step do not add up, and no step goes below the best Nordic benchmark.
No plan may claim more than 50% of an area's lung cancer deaths.

Stop rule: a measure is not bought if, added to the plan, it costs more than EUR 1,000,000 a year per death avoided a year at its central estimate. The limit is our assumption (Finland has no official one; it is roughly EUR 100,000 per life-year if ten life-years are gained). Such measures are listed as poor_value, and money may be left over.

Each action's numbers are what it adds to the actions ranked before it, so they add up to the plan total. Range, not a probability interval: lowest and highest value when every effect size and conversion assumption is moved together from its lower bound to its upper bound. The point estimate uses the published or central values.

Not counted: a symptom campaign or screening would also raise the share treated to cure by finding cancers earlier; the model counts them only through deaths avoided. Earlier life-prolonging drug treatment is not counted at all.
No budget share is reserved for any kind of measure (the 25% pathway rule of the earlier version is removed).
5000000.saturation_note_en: EUR 283,970 a year buys every measure that adds to this objective in North Savo. The remaining EUR 4,716,030 buys nothing more in the model: no remaining measure adds deaths avoided at an acceptable cost. Measures above the value limit are listed as poor_value under not_chosen.

goal3_link.note_en: Lung cancer causes about 93 deaths a year in North Savo (Finnish Cancer Registry, 2020-2024). This plan is modelled to avoid 1.1 of them a year (0.1-3.2), about 1.22%. Goal 3 of the cancer strategy asks for 10% lower cancer mortality (all cancers: from 13,288 deaths in 2022), so a plan of this size is a small part of it. The strategy also wants lung cancer survival at the level of Sweden and Norway: five-year survival is 13.2 points lower for Finnish men and 7.8 for women (2020-2024, NORDCAN). The share of patients treated with curative intent is the part of that gap a county can act on after diagnosis; this plan adds 1.5 such patients a year. Deaths avoided are modelled from stated assumptions, not observed.

5000000.budget_basis_en: Budget and costs are per year: running cost plus set-up cost spread over 5 years.

A treatment-access measure adds (its effect in percentage points / 100) x the county's patients a year. Every such effect is an assumption with a lower bound of zero: no trial has measured it.

Ceiling: in a county these measures together can add at most 50% of its measured shortfall to the curative share of the best quarter of counties, split into a surgery part and a radiotherapy part as on the care path. The rest is left for what they do not touch (stage at diagnosis, other illness, patient choice); no public table splits the shortfall by reason. A county at or above the best quarter gets no modelled gain.

Video MDT and the surgeon's second opinion count only where the county's own hospital is not a university hospital (not in Helsinki, the four Uusimaa counties, Southwest Finland, Pirkanmaa, North Savo, North Ostrobothnia; our reading of the collaborative-area structure). Travel support is scaled by road distance to the university hospital: 0 at 50 km, full at 200 km.

Where the care path carries a recording flag ('no treatment on record' far above and life-prolonging treatment far below the national share, or almost no drug treatment recorded), the recording audit is bought first. It adds no patients.
Measures that need a national decision (low-dose CT screening) are never bought from a county budget. They are listed under needs_national_decision with their own cost and effect, outside the budget.
Screening is counted from the people screened: participants x their lung cancer death rate without screening x the trial effect. The cost pays for the same participants.

Deaths avoided through treatment access = extra patients treated to cure x 0.15 (0.05-0.3) deaths within five years avoided per patient. This is an assumption, not a causal estimate (see parameters.json, curative_access).

Deaths avoided through days saved use the published hazard ratio per four weeks of delay (Hanna, BMJ 2020), for patients treated with curative intent only; its interval includes no effect, so a lower bound can be below zero.

Overlap: of several pre-diagnosis or mortality measures in one county, the k-th largest counts for 0.7^k of itself; two measures on the same pathway step do not add up, and no step goes below the best Nordic benchmark.
No plan may claim more than 50% of an area's lung cancer deaths.

Stop rule: a measure is not bought if, added to the plan, it costs more than EUR 1,000,000 a year per death avoided a year at its central estimate. The limit is our assumption (Finland has no official one; it is roughly EUR 100,000 per life-year if ten life-years are gained). Such measures are listed as poor_value, and money may be left over.

Each action's numbers are what it adds to the actions ranked before it, so they add up to the plan total. Range, not a probability interval: lowest and highest value when every effect size and conversion assumption is moved together from its lower bound to its upper bound. The point estimate uses the published or central values.

Not counted: a symptom campaign or screening would also raise the share treated to cure by finding cancers earlier; the model counts them only through deaths avoided. Earlier life-prolonging drug treatment is not counted at all.
No budget share is reserved for any kind of measure (the 25% pathway rule of the earlier version is removed).

rules_en: Budget and costs are per year: running cost plus set-up cost spread over 5 years. Costs are assumptions unless the action says otherwise.

Objective 'curative': the plan maximises extra patients a year treated with curative intent. The other objectives can be chosen: 'deaths' = deaths avoided a year (within five years, per yearly cohort of patients); 'gap' = extra patients a year treated with curative intent, counted only in counties below the national share and only up to it.
Method: buy the measure that adds most to the objective per euro, re-calculate what every other measure would add, and repeat until nothing more fits the budget or nothing more adds anything.
Measures with low-confidence evidence are ranked at 0.5 of their modelled value. They can still be bought; the numbers shown for them are not halved.
A treatment-access measure adds (its effect in percentage points / 100) x the county's patients a year. Every such effect is an assumption with a lower bound of zero: no trial has measured it.

Ceiling: in a county these measures together can add at most 50% of its measured shortfall to the curative share of the best quarter of counties, split into a surgery part and a radiotherapy part as on the care path. The rest is left for what they do not touch (stage at diagnosis, other illness, patient choice); no public table splits the shortfall by reason. A county at or above the best quarter gets no modelled gain.

Video MDT and the surgeon's second opinion count only where the county's own hospital is not a university hospital (not in Helsinki, the four Uusimaa counties, Southwest Finland, Pirkanmaa, North Savo, North Ostrobothnia; our reading of the collaborative-area structure). Travel support is scaled by road distance to the university hospital: 0 at 50 km, full at 200 km.

Where the care path carries a recording flag ('no treatment on record' far above and life-prolonging treatment far below the national share, or almost no drug treatment recorded), the recording audit is bought first. It adds no patients.
Measures that need a national decision (low-dose CT screening) are never bought from a county budget. They are listed under needs_national_decision with their own cost and effect, outside the budget.
Screening is counted from the people screened: participants x their lung cancer death rate without screening x the trial effect. The cost pays for the same participants.

Deaths avoided through treatment access = extra patients treated to cure x 0.15 (0.05-0.3) deaths within five years avoided per patient. This is an assumption, not a causal estimate (see parameters.json, curative_access).

Deaths avoided through days saved use the published hazard ratio per four weeks of delay (Hanna, BMJ 2020), for patients treated with curative intent only; its interval includes no effect, so a lower bound can be below zero.

Overlap: of several pre-diagnosis or mortality measures in one county, the k-th largest counts for 0.7^k of itself; two measures on the same pathway step do not add up, and no step goes below the best Nordic benchmark.
No plan may claim more than 50% of an area's lung cancer deaths.

Stop rule: a measure is not bought if, added to the plan, it costs more than EUR 1,000,000 a year per death avoided a year at its central estimate. The limit is our assumption (Finland has no official one; it is roughly EUR 100,000 per life-year if ten life-years are gained). Such measures are listed as poor_value, and money may be left over.

Each action's numbers are what it adds to the actions ranked before it, so they add up to the plan total. Range, not a probability interval: lowest and highest value when every effect size and conversion assumption is moved together from its lower bound to its upper bound. The point estimate uses the published or central values.

Not counted: a symptom campaign or screening would also raise the share treated to cure by finding cancers earlier; the model counts them only through deaths avoided. Earlier life-prolonging drug treatment is not counted at all.
No budget share is reserved for any kind of measure (the 25% pathway rule of the earlier version is removed).
500000.saturation_note_en: EUR 146,000 a year buys every measure that adds to this objective in North Karelia. The remaining EUR 354,000 buys nothing more in the model: the access measures are limited by the reachable part of the measured shortfall, not by money. To see what else the money could do, choose the deaths objective (pathway measures) or look at the measures that need a national decision.

goal3_link.note_en: Lung cancer causes about 81 deaths a year in North Karelia (Finnish Cancer Registry, 2020-2024). This plan is modelled to avoid 0.5 of them a year (0.0-1.2), about 0.57%. Goal 3 of the cancer strategy asks for 10% lower cancer mortality (all cancers: from 13,288 deaths in 2022), so a plan of this size is a small part of it. The strategy also wants lung cancer survival at the level of Sweden and Norway: five-year survival is 13.2 points lower for Finnish men and 7.8 for women (2020-2024, NORDCAN). The share of patients treated with curative intent is the part of that gap a county can act on after diagnosis; this plan adds 3.1 such patients a year. Deaths avoided are modelled from stated assumptions, not observed.

rules_en: Budget and costs are per year: running cost plus set-up cost spread over 5 years. Costs are assumptions unless the action says otherwise.

Objective 'curative': the plan maximises extra patients a year treated with curative intent. The other objectives can be chosen: 'deaths' = deaths avoided a year (within five years, per yearly cohort of patients); 'gap' = extra patients a year treated with curative intent, counted only in counties below the national share and only up to it.
Method: buy the measure that adds most to the objective per euro, re-calculate what every other measure would add, and repeat until nothing more fits the budget or nothing more adds anything.
Measures with low-confidence evidence are ranked at 0.5 of their modelled value. They can still be bought; the numbers shown for them are not halved.
A treatment-access measure adds (its effect in percentage points / 100) x the county's patients a year. Every such effect is an assumption with a lower bound of zero: no trial has measured it.

Ceiling: in a county these measures together can add at most 50% of its measured shortfall to the curative share of the best quarter of counties, split into a surgery part and a radiotherapy part as on the care path. The rest is left for what they do not touch (stage at diagnosis, other illness, patient choice); no public table splits the shortfall by reason. A county at or above the best quarter gets no modelled gain.

Video MDT and the surgeon's second opinion count only where the county's own hospital is not a university hospital (not in Helsinki, the four Uusimaa counties, Southwest Finland, Pirkanmaa, North Savo, North Ostrobothnia; our reading of the collaborative-area structure). Travel support is scaled by road distance to the university hospital: 0 at 50 km, full at 200 km.

Where the care path carries a recording flag ('no treatment on record' far above and life-prolonging treatment far below the national share, or almost no drug treatment recorded), the recording audit is bought first. It adds no patients.
Measures that need a national decision (low-dose CT screening) are never bought from a county budget. They are listed under needs_national_decision with their own cost and effect, outside the budget.
Screening is counted from the people screened: participants x their lung cancer death rate without screening x the trial effect. The cost pays for the same participants.

Deaths avoided through treatment access = extra patients treated to cure x 0.15 (0.05-0.3) deaths within five years avoided per patient. This is an assumption, not a causal estimate (see parameters.json, curative_access).

Deaths avoided through days saved use the published hazard ratio per four weeks of delay (Hanna, BMJ 2020), for patients treated with curative intent only; its interval includes no effect, so a lower bound can be below zero.

Overlap: of several pre-diagnosis or mortality measures in one county, the k-th largest counts for 0.7^k of itself; two measures on the same pathway step do not add up, and no step goes below the best Nordic benchmark.
No plan may claim more than 50% of an area's lung cancer deaths.

Stop rule: a measure is not bought if, added to the plan, it costs more than EUR 1,000,000 a year per death avoided a year at its central estimate. The limit is our assumption (Finland has no official one; it is roughly EUR 100,000 per life-year if ten life-years are gained). Such measures are listed as poor_value, and money may be left over.

Each action's numbers are what it adds to the actions ranked before it, so they add up to the plan total. Range, not a probability interval: lowest and highest value when every effect size and conversion assumption is moved together from its lower bound to its upper bound. The point estimate uses the published or central values.

Not counted: a symptom campaign or screening would also raise the share treated to cure by finding cancers earlier; the model counts them only through deaths avoided. Earlier life-prolonging drug treatment is not counted at all.
No budget share is reserved for any kind of measure (the 25% pathway rule of the earlier version is removed).
2000000.saturation_note_en: EUR 146,000 a year buys every measure that adds to this objective in North Karelia. The remaining EUR 1,854,000 buys nothing more in the model: the access measures are limited by the reachable part of the measured shortfall, not by money. To see what else the money could do, choose the deaths objective (pathway measures) or look at the measures that need a national decision.

goal3_link.note_en: Lung cancer causes about 81 deaths a year in North Karelia (Finnish Cancer Registry, 2020-2024). This plan is modelled to avoid 0.5 of them a year (0.0-1.2), about 0.57%. Goal 3 of the cancer strategy asks for 10% lower cancer mortality (all cancers: from 13,288 deaths in 2022), so a plan of this size is a small part of it. The strategy also wants lung cancer survival at the level of Sweden and Norway: five-year survival is 13.2 points lower for Finnish men and 7.8 for women (2020-2024, NORDCAN). The share of patients treated with curative intent is the part of that gap a county can act on after diagnosis; this plan adds 3.1 such patients a year. Deaths avoided are modelled from stated assumptions, not observed.

Measures with low-confidence evidence are ranked at 0.5 of their modelled value. They can still be bought; the numbers shown for them are not halved.
A treatment-access measure adds (its effect in percentage points / 100) x the county's patients a year. Every such effect is an assumption with a lower bound of zero: no trial has measured it.

Ceiling: in a county these measures together can add at most 50% of its measured shortfall to the curative share of the best quarter of counties, split into a surgery part and a radiotherapy part as on the care path. The rest is left for what they do not touch (stage at diagnosis, other illness, patient choice); no public table splits the shortfall by reason. Video MDT and the surgeon's second opinion count only where the county's own hospital is not a university hospital (not in Helsinki, the four Uusimaa counties, Southwest Finland, Pirkanmaa, North Savo, North Ostrobothnia; our reading of the collaborative-area structure). Where the care path carries a recording flag ('no treatment on record' far above and life-prolonging treatment far below the national share, or almost no drug treatment recorded), the recording audit is bought first. It adds no patients.
Measures that need a national decision (low-dose CT screening) are never bought from a county budget. They are listed under needs_national_decision with their own cost and effect, outside the budget.
Screening is counted from the people screened: participants x their lung cancer death rate without screening x the trial effect. The cost pays for the same participants.

Deaths avoided through treatment access = extra patients treated to cure x 0.15 (0.05-0.3) deaths within five years avoided per patient. This is an assumption, not a causal estimate (see parameters.json, curative_access).

rules_en: Budget and costs are per year: running cost plus set-up cost spread over 5 years. Costs are assumptions unless the action says otherwise.

Objective 'curative': the plan maximises extra patients a year treated with curative intent. The other objectives can be chosen: 'deaths' = deaths avoided a year (within five years, per yearly cohort of patients); 'gap' = extra patients a year treated with curative intent, counted only in counties below the national share and only up to it.
Method: buy the measure that adds most to the objective per euro, re-calculate what every other measure would add, and repeat until nothing more fits the budget or nothing more adds anything.
Measures with low-confidence evidence are ranked at 0.5 of their modelled value. They can still be bought; the numbers shown for them are not halved.
A treatment-access measure adds (its effect in percentage points / 100) x the county's patients a year. Every such effect is an assumption with a lower bound of zero: no trial has measured it.

Ceiling: in a county these measures together can add at most 50% of its measured shortfall to the curative share of the best quarter of counties, split into a surgery part and a radiotherapy part as on the care path. The rest is left for what they do not touch (stage at diagnosis, other illness, patient choice); no public table splits the shortfall by reason. A county at or above the best quarter gets no modelled gain.

Video MDT and the surgeon's second opinion count only where the county's own hospital is not a university hospital (not in Helsinki, the four Uusimaa counties, Southwest Finland, Pirkanmaa, North Savo, North Ostrobothnia; our reading of the collaborative-area structure). Travel support is scaled by road distance to the university hospital: 0 at 50 km, full at 200 km.

Where the care path carries a recording flag ('no treatment on record' far above and life-prolonging treatment far below the national share, or almost no drug treatment recorded), the recording audit is bought first. It adds no patients.
Measures that need a national decision (low-dose CT screening) are never bought from a county budget. They are listed under needs_national_decision with their own cost and effect, outside the budget.
Screening is counted from the people screened: participants x their lung cancer death rate without screening x the trial effect. The cost pays for the same participants.

Deaths avoided through treatment access = extra patients treated to cure x 0.15 (0.05-0.3) deaths within five years avoided per patient. This is an assumption, not a causal estimate (see parameters.json, curative_access).

Deaths avoided through days saved use the published hazard ratio per four weeks of delay (Hanna, BMJ 2020), for patients treated with curative intent only; its interval includes no effect, so a lower bound can be below zero.

Overlap: of several pre-diagnosis or mortality measures in one county, the k-th largest counts for 0.7^k of itself; two measures on the same pathway step do not add up, and no step goes below the best Nordic benchmark.
No plan may claim more than 50% of an area's lung cancer deaths.

Stop rule: a measure is not bought if, added to the plan, it costs more than EUR 1,000,000 a year per death avoided a year at its central estimate. The limit is our assumption (Finland has no official one; it is roughly EUR 100,000 per life-year if ten life-years are gained). Such measures are listed as poor_value, and money may be left over.

Each action's numbers are what it adds to the actions ranked before it, so they add up to the plan total. Range, not a probability interval: lowest and highest value when every effect size and conversion assumption is moved together from its lower bound to its upper bound. The point estimate uses the published or central values.

Not counted: a symptom campaign or screening would also raise the share treated to cure by finding cancers earlier; the model counts them only through deaths avoided. Earlier life-prolonging drug treatment is not counted at all.
No budget share is reserved for any kind of measure (the 25% pathway rule of the earlier version is removed).
100000.saturation_note_en: Not saturated: the cheapest measure that would still add something (Fitness test and training before anyone is ruled too frail for curative treatment) needs EUR 27,500 a year; EUR 5,000 is left.

goal3_link.note_en: Lung cancer causes about 81 deaths a year in North Karelia (Finnish Cancer Registry, 2020-2024). This plan is modelled to avoid 0.3 of them a year (0.0-1.0), about 0.43%. Goal 3 of the cancer strategy asks for 10% lower cancer mortality (all cancers: from 13,288 deaths in 2022), so a plan of this size is a small part of it. The strategy also wants lung cancer survival at the level of Sweden and Norway: five-year survival is 13.2 points lower for Finnish men and 7.8 for women (2020-2024, NORDCAN). The share of patients treated with curative intent is the part of that gap a county can act on after diagnosis; this plan adds 2.3 such patients a year. Deaths avoided are modelled from stated assumptions, not observed.

totals.gap_note_en: gap_closed_pct = extra patients treated to cure, counted up to each county's measured shortfall against the national share, divided by that shortfall. Arithmetic on a modelled gain and a measured shortfall; None where the county is at or above the national share.
totals.deaths_basis_en: Deaths within five years avoided per yearly cohort of patients; modelled, not observed. The part from treatment access rests on an assumed 0.15 deaths avoided per extra patient treated to cure.
totals.days_saved_note_en: Secondary: average days saved per patient on the estimated clock (central estimate). Not a headline number; access measures save no days.
totals.interval_en: Range, not a probability interval: lowest and highest value when every effect size and conversion assumption is moved together from its lower bound to its upper bound. The point estimate uses the published or central values.
totals.method_en: Greedy on extra patients a year treated with curative intent per euro, re-evaluated after every pick. Budget and costs are per year: running cost plus set-up cost spread over 5 years. Every number is modelled; treatment-access effects are assumptions with a lower bound of zero.
